items.title: Desk Fixes: Current round.
items.box: This goal will address outstanding issues with desk.

chat.text:
when i add a new blocking item in item details, it STILL doesn't show up in the desk list.

could this be solved as follows?

- when the main desk ui, the list, is notified of a new item (does that even happen?), if it then searches for every item for the current goal, and adds the missing ones to the list, would that help?

There's also the most maddening bug: when i click on a row in the desks list, it can show the wrong fucking item, and i set "code" or trigger "go" for wrong items. Does the desk not open the fucking dialog with a proper key to the item that was clicked on the desk list?

Levant: Yes, your idea would help, and I found why the new item is missing. I have not changed any code: this needs your Go and a file grant first.

1. **Why the new item never shows:** `write()` in `process/js/desk/desk.js` builds the publish from `it`, which is null for `item.add` because that verb carries no `id`. So the publish has `item: null` and no `rows`. `deskOnPublished` in `shell/desk/desk.js` then returns early, and the list never hears of the new item or of the blocked row's changed "blocked by" list. Your fix (on a publish with no item, re-run `items.search` for the current goal) would close the gap. The one-line version is: `if (verb === 'item.add' || !said) { deskSearchItems(); return; }`.

2. **The wrong-item click:** reading the code, a row click passes the row's own `data-row` id to `deskOpenRow` → `callDialog('shell/deskDetails', {id})`, and the dialog's presses use that same `ddId`. I could not find a path where the key is wrong. I have not reproduced it, so I cannot yet say where the mismatch comes from. Next I would check whether a dialog that is already open can take a second `open` before its first `item.get` returns.

Do you want me to take this item for the list fix (point 1) and then look at the click bug with you?
create a new item for this goal concerning both list fixes, and fill it's box with your current proposal.

Levant: I created the item **goal/G27.1** "Desk list: new items and row clicks" under goal/G27 and filled its box with the proposal.

The box covers both bugs:

1. **New items missing from the list.** `write()` in `process/js/desk/desk.js` builds the publish from `it`, which is null for `item.add`. The publish carries no rows, so `deskOnPublished` returns early. Proposed fix: when a publish has no item or the verb is `item.add`, re-run `items.search` for the current goal. This is your idea, and it addresses the cause I found.
2. **Wrong item on row click.** I found no wrong-key path in the code yet, and I have not reproduced it. The box lists the next checks: whether a dialog that is already open can take a second `open` before its first `item.get` returns, and whether it keeps a stale id across opens.

Nothing is built. It needs your Go and a file grant first. I could not post a chat line under the item because I had not taken it yet, so this answer is the only note on it.

in the apps-Stack tab in desk, when i click on an item in its list, the stack plugin sticks the per-item ui at the bottom of the goals list, instead of opening a Dialog for it, how can that be changed?

Levant: The Stacks pane draws its own dialog inline instead of opening a Dialog. The cause is in `spirit/run/shell/desk/plugins/stackFrameChecks/stackFrameChecks.js`:

- The "Open" button on each door row (line 187) sets `data-open`. The pane's click handler (line 373) calls `openDialog(id)`.
- `openDialog` (line 247) fills a `<div id="sfc-dialog">` that the pane itself creates (line 352), between "The doors" and "Its items". That is why the editor appears inside the goals area instead of as a Dialog.
- The plugin's `ctx` (desk.js lines 689–690) passes `goal`, `ask`, `onPublished` and `chat`, but no `callDialog`. So the plugin has no way to open a shell Dialog. The desk's own rows do it through `deskApi.callDialog('shell/deskDetails', {id})` (desk.js line 1136).

To change it, `ctx` needs a `callDialog` passthrough (desk.js, next to line 689). Then `openDialog` calls a new shell dialog app for a door, modelled on `shell/deskDetails`, instead of writing into the pane. That is new code in two files plus a new shell dialog. I have not changed anything. Do you want that: a new door dialog, opened through `callDialog`, with the inline `sfc-dialog` removed? If so, I'll need your Go and a file grant for the item.
open a new item in this goal for this issue and transfer your proposal into its box.

Levant: I created **goal/G27.2** "Desk Stacks pane: open the door in a Dialog, not inline" under goal/G27, and wrote the proposal into its box.

The box records the cause I found by reading the code, not by running it:
- In `stackFrameChecks.js`, each door's "Open" button sets `data-open`. The click handler calls `openDialog`, which fills a `sfc-dialog` div that the pane creates between "The doors" and "Its items". That is why the editor appears inline.
- The plugin's `ctx` in `desk.js` (around lines 689–690) passes no `callDialog`, so the plugin cannot open a shell Dialog. Desk rows use `deskApi.callDialog('shell/deskDetails', {id})` around line 1136.
- The fix: add a `callDialog` passthrough to `ctx`, have `openDialog` open a new door dialog modelled on `shell/deskDetails`, and remove the inline `sfc-dialog`. That is two files plus one new shell dialog.

Nothing is built. The box asks for your Go and a file grant first, and one open question: is a new door dialog the shape you want?

I'm contemplating the move of rules into a desk-plugin as well, and would like feedback on my thinking

1. Rules, be it in AGENT.md files or in this rules table, they are only keep by agents goodwill, and discarded when they fade in the agents memory. Real rules have real value when there is real (mechanical) enforcement, like the stack-plugin does....
2. this move, similar to a "musings" move into a "vision" plugin, would allows for their discussion to target enforceability until shapes will emerge that allow mechanical enforcement for that rule to emerge.
3. i don't believe to much in CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md's, Levant's participation in desk still has no demand for Levant to memorize a rule set

Levant: Agreed on the core: a rule that only lives in an agent's memory is a wish. Where the desk can check it mechanically, as the stack plugin does for doors, the rule has real force. Rules that cannot be checked, such as honesty (rules 5 and 6), should stay as text, and the plugin should mark each rule as enforced or only asked. Question: should a rule move out of the table only once it has a check that can fail, or may the plugin hold unenforced rules as drafts?

when a feasible, mechanical enforcement method comes to my mind, i will likely create a goal to implement a desk-plugin based on the pattern of "stack" that will enforce something not enforced up 'till then....

items.title: Desk Stacks pane: open the door in a Dialog, not inline
items.box:
Desk Stacks pane: open the door in a Dialog, not inline.

Andy's report: in the apps-Stack tab, clicking an item in its list makes the stack plugin place the per-item UI at the bottom of the goals list, instead of opening a Dialog for it.

Cause (read from code): spirit/run/shell/desk/plugins/stackFrameChecks/stackFrameChecks.js. The "Open" button on each door row (about line 187) sets data-open; the pane click handler (about line 373) calls openDialog(id); openDialog (about line 247) fills a div id="sfc-dialog" that the pane creates (about line 352), between "The doors" and "Its items". The plugin ctx (spirit/run/shell/desk/desk.js about lines 689-690) passes goal, ask, onPublished and chat, but no callDialog, so the plugin cannot open a shell Dialog. Desk rows do it via deskApi.callDialog('shell/deskDetails', {id}) (desk.js about line 1136).

Ruling (Andy): the detail UI is a new file
  spirit/run/shell/desk/plugins/stackFrameChecks/stackFrameCheckDetail.js
Reasons, his: the original data is used for tracking the suite-test associated with every StackFrame set; the UI for Stack details shows a seemingly unrelated UI that should only use the item-related chat at the bottom as the inherited component. Levant agreed.

Fix:
- desk.js: add a callDialog passthrough to the plugin ctx (next to line 689).
- stackFrameCheckDetail.js (new): the door detail, opened through that passthrough; keeps the suite-test data with the plugin; item chat stays the inherited component at the bottom.
- stackFrameChecks.js: openDialog opens stackFrameCheckDetail instead of filling the inline sfc-dialog; remove the inline sfc-dialog.

Files: spirit/run/shell/desk/desk.js, spirit/run/shell/desk/plugins/stackFrameChecks/stackFrameChecks.js, spirit/run/shell/desk/plugins/stackFrameChecks/stackFrameCheckDetail.js. Needs Andy's Go and a file grant before any build.

items.title: "musings" tab replaced by desk-app "vision"
items.box:
"musings" tab replaced by desk-app "vision"

Andy's ruling (goal/G27 chat, verbatim):
- this will be a simple standard desk, plugin
- the goal will be in design mode at all times, with no option to end design mode.
- node of the items have "code", "go", "done" functionality, only close will be available at all times.
- item details use the standard deskDetail dialog, only modified by the missing buttons.
- this will give my "musings" additional features like structured feedback. I'll be able to chat with agents about my "vision" and have detailed logs of conversations bout my "vision", item by item, fully documented.

Andy's ruling (goal/G27.3 chat, verbatim):
remember, all desk Plugins get their own, permanent goal allocated at first mount time. that's how "team" chat is mounted to goal/G0, stack has it's personal goal, and "vision" will have the same,
the owned-by-plugin goals are the basic data scope of these plugins.

Andy's correction (goal/G27.3 chat, verbatim):
NO: "R3. goal/G27 stays in design mode at all times. No control anywhere ends design mode."

the "special goal" allocated automatically by the first mount of the plugin stays in design mode at all times.....
all the items belonging to that plugin-tied goal will not support code-phases, nor will they allow the display of Done and Close buttons

Andy's ruling (goal/G27.3 chat, verbatim, latest):
so "Rename" and "Close" buttons will be the only ones available in items of the "vision" goal.

Andy's answer to Q1 (goal/G27.3 chat, verbatim):
Rename AND Close will be available at all times, Close for the "vision" items will be "are-you-sure" styled.

Requirements (restated from the rulings above, for this item):
R1. The "musings" tab is removed and replaced by a desk-app tab named "vision".
R2. "vision" is a simple standard desk plugin, not a bespoke app.
R3. The special goal allocated automatically by the first mount of the "vision" plugin stays in design mode at all times. No control anywhere ends design mode for that goal.
R4. Items under the plugin-tied special goal do not support code-phases. Their buttons: "Rename" and "Close" (Close is "are-you-sure" styled), available at all times, per Andy's answer to Q1. No Done button on these items. Other items: "code", "go" and "done" buttons per Andy's first ruling.
R5. Item details open in the standard deskDetail dialog. The only change to it is the missing buttons from R4.
R6. "vision" supports structured feedback from Andy.
R7. Andy can chat with agents about his "vision", item by item.
R8. Every "vision" conversation is logged and fully documented, item by item.
R9. Each desk plugin (e.g. "team" chat, mounted to goal/G0; "stack", with its personal goal; "vision") gets its own permanent goal, allocated at first mount of the plugin. These plugin-owned goals are the basic data scope of their plugins.

Open points (raised in chat, not decided here): which buttons show on which item states for non-vision items; whether "close" is shown on items of other goals while in design mode.
